claims.text: The company manufactures and markets branded chocolate, confectionery and salty-snack products sold mainly to grocery, mass-market and convenience retailers across North America and internationally, with revenue earned through wholesale product sales.
Full-year 2022 net sales were $10,419.3 million, up 16.1%, with organic constant-currency growth of 12.0% made up of 8.0 points of net price realization and 4.0 points of volume/mix.
The company's 2023 full-year outlook calls for net sales growth of 6%-8% and adjusted earnings-per-share growth of 9%-11%, versus 2022's 16.1% sales growth and 18.5% adjusted EPS growth.

The North America Salty Snacks segment grew full-year net sales 85.3% (helped by 2021 acquisitions) while the International segment's full-year income turned to a 12.6% margin, up from 10.1% a year earlier.

For 2023 the company guided capital expenditures of approximately $800-900 million, driven by core confection capacity expansion and a digital-infrastructure build including a new enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.
Management said 2022 results were achieved despite record inflation, continued supply-chain disruptions and macroeconomic uncertainty for consumers.
2023 guidance embeds interest expense of approximately $145-155 million, which the company said reflects a higher interest-rate environment.
Full-year 2022 net sales and adjusted EPS grew 16.1% and 18.5% respectively even as management cited record input-cost inflation, evidence of realized pricing power.
2023 guidance of 6%-8% sales growth and 9%-11% adjusted EPS growth, while slower than 2022, is still above-average growth for a consumer-staples guidance range.
The North America Salty Snacks segment's fourth-quarter margin expanded 840 basis points to 20.8% as the 2021 acquisitions integrated, adding a second profit engine alongside core confectionery.
2023 guidance itself embeds a deceleration to single-digit sales growth and continued cost pressure, alongside higher planned interest expense and capital spending.
Reported gross margin already declined 30 basis points to 43.2% in the fourth quarter of 2022, driven by broad-based cost-of-goods inflation that outpaced price realization.

Planned 2023 capital expenditure of $800-900 million and interest expense of $145-155 million represent a step up in cash outflow that could pressure free cash flow if growth decelerates faster than guided.

U.S. candy, mint and gum retail category share declined 54 basis points in the twelve weeks ended January 1, 2023, even as price-led retail sales rose 10.7%, due to category mix headwinds and capacity constraints.
